newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine water firm puts dispute on hold.
newsitem.headline: Argentine water firm puts dispute on hold.

text.p: Cie Generale des Eaux unit Aguas del Aconquija has agreed to put on hold a suit against the government of the Argentine province of Tucuman and go into talks in a bid to solve their dispute, a local news agency reported Tuesday.

The firm, which also has Spanish shareholders, has agreed to suspend the case it presented before an international investments court in Washington and open talks with the Tucuman government, the private DyN news agency said.
Tucuman's Deputy Governor Raul Topa said he expected negotiations to start sometime next week.

Aguas was privatized in July 1995, but the Tucuman government accused its new Spanish and French owners of rendering an inefficient service. In August 1996 the two sides signed a new contract, but it was rejected by the provincial legislature.
Late last year Aguas declared its interests were jeopardized and took the case to a dispute settlements court in Washington.
